name: dialog
title: Dialog
description: A window overlaid on either the primary window or another dialog window, rendering the content underneath inert.
usageSnippet:
<Dialog>
  <@trigger|props|>
    <button ...props>Open</button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>Are you absolutely sure?</@title>
  <@description>
    This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account
    and remove your data from our servers.
  </@description>
</Dialog>

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Human readable label for the dialog, in event the dialog title is not rendered

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Whether to close the dialog when the escape key is pressed

props.name: closeOnInteractOutside
props.description: Whether to close the dialog when the outside is clicked

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
The initial open state of the dialog when rendered.
Use when you don't need to control the open state of the dialog.

props.name: defaultTriggerValue
props.description:
The initial active trigger value when rendered.
Use when you don't need to control the active trigger value.

props.name: finalFocusEl
props.description: Element to receive focus when the dialog is closed

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the elements in the dialog. Useful for composition.

props.name: initialFocusEl
props.description: Element to receive focus when the dialog is opened

props.name: modal
props.description: Whether to prevent pointer interaction outside the element and hide all content below it

props.name: open
props.description: The controlled open state of the dialog

props.name: persistentElements
props.description:
Returns the persistent elements that:
- should not have pointer-events disabled
- should not trigger the dismiss event

props.name: preventScroll
props.description: Whether to prevent scrolling behind the dialog when it's opened

props.name: restoreFocus
props.description: Whether to restore focus to the element that had focus before the dialog was opened

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Show the top-right close button. Defaults to true.

props.name: trapFocus
props.description: Whether to trap focus inside the dialog when it's opened

events.name: onEscapeKeyDown
events.description: Function called when the escape key is pressed

events.name: onFocusOutside
events.description: Function called when the focus is moved outside the component

events.name: onInteractOutside
events.description: Function called when an interaction happens outside the component

events.name: onOpenChange
events.description: Function to call when the dialog's open state changes

events.name: onPointerDownOutside
events.description: Function called when the pointer is pressed down outside the component

events.name: onRequestDismiss
events.description: Function called when this layer is closed due to a parent layer being closed

events.name: onTriggerValueChange
events.description: Function to call when the active trigger changes

keyboard.description: Opens the dialog when focus is on the trigger.
Cycles focus among the dialog's focusable elements; focus is trapped inside while open.

accessibilityNotes: Rendered with `role="dialog"` per the [WAI-ARIA Dialog (Modal) Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/); the title and description are linked to the content via `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`, generated automatically from `@title`/`@description`.
Focus moves into the dialog on open and is trapped there until it closes; it's restored to the trigger element on close.

Both the Escape key and clicking outside the content close the dialog by default (`closeOnEscape`/`closeOnInteractOutside`, both `true`) — unlike `AlertDialog`, which disables both so the user must make an explicit choice.

examples.title: No Close Button
examples.source:
import Dialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/dialog/dialog.marko";
import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";

<Dialog showCloseButton=false>
  <@trigger|props|>
    <Button type="button" ...props variant="outline">No Close Button</Button>
  </@trigger>
  <@title>No Close Button</@title>
  <@description>This dialog doesn't have a close button in the top-right corner.</@description>
</Dialog>
examples.description: Set `showCloseButton={false}` to hide the top-right close button.

examples.description: The `dir` prop is a native attribute pass-through — set it on `<Dialog>` to flip logical-property layout and typography for right-to-left languages. Every RTL example on this site does it the same way: a `dir="rtl"` wrapper plus Arabic labels.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.source:
import Dialog from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/dialog/dialog.marko"; import Button from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/button/button.marko";
{ open = next; } > <@trigger|props|> <@title>Controlled dialog <@description>This dialog's open state is held in the parent and can be toggled from outside too. <@footer> open: ${String(open)}
examples.description: Zag machines are controlled: an `open` prop without a change handler never moves. Pair it with `openChange`.

composition: `<Dialog>` is one file exposing upstream's tree as slots: `@trigger` (render-prop, receives the trigger props to spread onto your own element — never nest a `<button>` inside it), `@title`, `@description`, the tag's own body (the content between the header and footer), and `@footer` (actions row). `@title`/`@description` are optional but recommended: omitting both drops the generated `dialog-header` wrapper entirely, and either one alone renders without the other. `showCloseButton` (default `true`) controls the generated top-right close button.
